t: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent. Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace, so a failure leaves it empty. Several actions reset it; others do not. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent. Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace, so a failure leaves it empty. Several actions reset it; others do not.

t: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names. Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import, can change other registry keys. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names. Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import, can change other registry keys.

t: Applying a policy, from the settings window or a script, clears its stored values or comment before the new ones are read or written. A failure, such as a drop-down with no choice, leaves the policy empty or half set and reports little. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Applying a policy, from the settings window or a script, clears its stored values or comment before the new ones are read or written. A failure, such as a drop-down with no choice, leaves the policy empty or half set and reports little.

t: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden. An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost, and turning on the comment filter then fails with an unhandled error. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden. An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost, and turning on the comment filter then fails with an unhandled error.

t: Enabling a policy with a list option the person never opened writes that option with no list. The list stays empty until the list editor is used or the source holds one, and nothing checks it. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Enabling a policy with a list option the person never opened writes that option with no list. The list stays empty until the list editor is used or the source holds one, and nothing checks it.

t: For an administrator, the program unpacks a package it never verified and then makes Administrators owner of the typed destination with full control, so a compromised source would be trusted with that folder. Releasing or running the system depends on manual or missing steps
l: For an administrator, the program unpacks a package it never verified and then makes Administrators owner of the typed destination with full control, so a compromised source would be trusted with that folder.

t: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values. A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values. A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.

t: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names. The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches. Someone can read or change what they should not
l: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names. The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.

t: Policy files and REG files are saved by overwriting in place. A failure partway leaves a truncated or damaged file, with no copy of the old one. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Policy files and REG files are saved by overwriting in place. A failure partway leaves a truncated or damaged file, with no copy of the old one.

t: Policy template and comment XML files are read with default settings and no stated limit on external references. The folders or domain share they come from may be writable by others, and whether external entities resolve depends on the framework default. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Policy template and comment XML files are read with default settings and no stated limit on external references. The folders or domain share they come from may be writable by others, and whether external entities resolve depends on the framework default.

t: Results of requesting Windows privileges and loading a user registry file are discarded. The person learns a source cannot be saved, or silently gets an empty read-only source, never why. A refused privilege passes silently and fails later with an unrelated error. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: Results of requesting Windows privileges and loading a user registry file are discarded. The person learns a source cannot be saved, or silently gets an empty read-only source, never why. A refused privilege passes silently and fails later with an unrelated error.

t: Saving a local or per-user policy writes the policy file first and the version file second. A failure on the second step, or a malformed version line that truncates the version file, leaves new settings with an old or damaged version, which Group Policy clients use to detect change. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Saving a local or per-user policy writes the policy file first and the version file second. A failure on the second step, or a malformed version line that truncates the version file, leaves new settings with an old or damaged version, which Group Policy clients use to detect change.

t: Saving reports its result poorly. One handler covers both sources without saying which failed, success is shown even when nothing was writable, and the result of the Group Policy refresh request is ignored, so a person may be told a policy applied when it did not. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: Saving reports its result poorly. One handler covers both sources without saying which failed, success is shown even when nothing was writable, and the result of the Group Policy refresh request is ignored, so a person may be told a policy applied when it did not.

t: Saving writes the computer source first and the user source second, with no rollback. If the user save fails, the computer policies are already on disk, yet the person sees only a failure and the chosen sources are not remembered. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Saving writes the computer source first and the user source second, with no rollback. If the user save fails, the computer policies are already on disk, yet the person sees only a failure and the chosen sources are not remembered.

t: Template and comment XML files, read from a chosen folder or the domain share, are loaded with default settings and no stated limit on external references. Whether those resolve rests on the framework default, which the code does not settle. If they do, a crafted file on a writable share could read local files. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Template and comment XML files, read from a chosen folder or the domain share, are loaded with default settings and no stated limit on external references. Whether those resolve rests on the framework default, which the code does not settle. If they do, a crafted file on a writable share could read local files.

t: Text typed by the person, a user identifier or a language code, is used unchecked as part of a folder path. Path characters redirect where policy and version files are created or which folder is searched for definition text, using the person's own rights. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Text typed by the person, a user identifier or a language code, is used unchecked as part of a folder path. Path characters redirect where policy and version files are created or which folder is searched for definition text, using the person's own rights.

t: The download accepts what it is given without checks: the package is unpacked with no signature or hash check, and the destination is any folder typed. For an administrator the files written also get their access rules reset. The package address is fixed HTTPS, so the package gap matters only if that channel is compromised. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: The download accepts what it is given without checks: the package is unpacked with no signature or hash check, and the destination is any folder typed. For an administrator the files written also get their access rules reset. The package address is fixed HTTPS, so the package gap matters only if that channel is compromised.

t: The download destination is free text and never checked as a policy definitions folder. A wrong existing folder typed or browsed to, which needs an administrator to change the default, has its ownership taken and its same-named files deleted and replaced. A folder that does not exist is simply created. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: The download destination is free text and never checked as a policy definitions folder. A wrong existing folder typed or browsed to, which needs an administrator to change the default, has its ownership taken and its same-named files deleted and replaced. A folder that does not exist is simply created.

t: The downloaded Microsoft template package is run through the Windows installer tool with no signature, publisher or hash check, only a secure address. The tool processes the package before anything is verified, so a compromised channel or address delivers altered files for the template folder. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: The downloaded Microsoft template package is run through the Windows installer tool with no signature, publisher or hash check, only a secure address. The tool processes the package before anything is verified, so a compromised channel or address delivers altered files for the template folder.

t: The Microsoft template package is unpacked with no hash or signature check, so a tampered or substituted package would have its files moved into the policy template folder. The address is a fixed Microsoft link, which limits exposure to a compromised source or channel. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: The Microsoft template package is unpacked with no hash or signature check, so a tampered or substituted package would have its files moved into the policy template folder. The address is a fixed Microsoft link, which limits exposure to a compromised source or channel.

t: The name of a value added in the raw policy editor is not checked. An empty name hides the key's marker, and names that begin with deletion prefixes or equal the delete-values name are read back as deletion or clearing instructions. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: The name of a value added in the raw policy editor is not checked. An empty name hides the key's marker, and names that begin with deletion prefixes or equal the delete-values name are read back as deletion or clearing instructions.

t: The program allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1 as well as 1.2 for every web request, which is only the template download, to keep Vista working. A server or on-path party forcing an old protocol would be accepted. The download address is fixed HTTPS. Data is protected by weak or fixed encryption
l: The program allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1 as well as 1.2 for every web request, which is only the template download, to keep Vista working. A server or on-path party forcing an old protocol would be accepted. The download address is fixed HTTPS.

t: The template download deletes each existing file before moving the new one in. A failure midway leaves the destination partly replaced, and the scratch folder with the downloaded package stays in the person's local data. Only the failed step is reported. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: The template download deletes each existing file before moving the new one in. A failure midway leaves the destination partly replaced, and the scratch folder with the downloaded package stays in the person's local data. Only the failed step is reported.

t: The template download, run as administrator, takes ownership of the destination folder and its existing language subfolders, grants Administrators full control and replaces same-named files; a missing folder is created. This happens to the system definitions folder even on the default path, not only when another folder is typed. Someone can read or change what they should not
l: The template download, run as administrator, takes ownership of the destination folder and its existing language subfolders, grants Administrators full control and replaces same-named files; a missing folder is created. This happens to the system definitions folder even on the default path, not only when another folder is typed.

t: The template download, when run as administrator, takes ownership of whatever folder is typed or browsed to, grants Administrators full control, and deletes and replaces same-named files there. The folder defaults to the standard template folder but is not checked, so a wrong existing folder has its ownership and permissions changed. Someone can read or change what they should not
l: The template download, when run as administrator, takes ownership of whatever folder is typed or browsed to, grants Administrators full control, and deletes and replaces same-named files there. The folder defaults to the standard template folder but is not checked, so a wrong existing folder has its ownership and permissions changed.

t: Unsaved policy changes are lost without warning for sources backed by a policy file. Opening other sources or exiting closes them with no prompt. Registry sources apply at once, so lose nothing. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Unsaved policy changes are lost without warning for sources backed by a policy file. Opening other sources or exiting closes them with no prompt. Registry sources apply at once, so lose nothing.

t: Values supplied for a policy's settings, by a person or a script, are written without checks. Numbers are forced to unsigned 32-bit and text is stored as given, ignoring any minimum, maximum or length in the definition. A failure leaves earlier settings written, with no undo. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Values supplied for a policy's settings, by a person or a script, are written without checks. Numbers are forced to unsigned 32-bit and text is stored as given, ignoring any minimum, maximum or length in the definition. A failure leaves earlier settings written, with no undo.

t: What the template download moves into the policy template folder is whatever the unpacked package holds. With no check of the package, a tampered or substituted one replaces the installed templates, which the program then loads as trusted definitions. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: What the template download moves into the policy template folder is whatever the unpacked package holds. With no check of the package, a tampered or substituted one replaces the installed templates, which the program then loads as trusted definitions.

t: When a download, install or export fails, the person sees only the step that failed, not the cause, with no retry. A finished install can be reported as a failure when cleanup fails, leaving the new folder unloaded and unpacked files behind. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: When a download, install or export fails, the person sees only the step that failed, not the cause, with no retry. A finished install can be reported as a failure when cleanup fails, leaving the new folder unloaded and unpacked files behind.

t: When rights or a per-user registry file cannot be obtained, the results are discarded. The person is told a source cannot be modified or saved, never why, and can keep editing an empty in-memory source that is never written. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: When rights or a per-user registry file cannot be obtained, the results are discarded. The person is told a source cannot be modified or saved, never why, and can keep editing an empty in-memory source that is never written.

t: A failure to open or create the saved-settings registry area is silently swallowed. The program then runs without remembering anything and the person is never told. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: A failure to open or create the saved-settings registry area is silently swallowed. The program then runs without remembering anything and the person is never told.

t: A typed user identifier is joined into the per-user policy folder path with no check, so a crafted value can point the written policy and version files at another folder. It acts only with the person's own rights. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: A typed user identifier is joined into the per-user policy folder path with no check, so a crafted value can point the written policy and version files at another folder. It acts only with the person's own rights.

t: Changing or loading policy sources has no error handling. Sources are replaced one by one, so a failure leaves a mix or an empty workspace with an unhandled error. A start-up fallback still presets the failed sources, and a missing registry location stops a POL export. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: Changing or loading policy sources has no error handling. Sources are replaced one by one, so a failure leaves a mix or an empty workspace with an unhandled error. A start-up fallback still presets the failed sources, and a missing registry location stops a POL export.

t: Each template states the minimum text-file revision it needs and each text file states its own, but nothing compares them. A template can be paired with text too old for it. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Each template states the minimum text-file revision it needs and each text file states its own, but nothing compares them. A template can be paired with text too old for it.

t: Escape in the raw policy editor looks like a cancel, but every edit has already changed the loaded policy source and the caller ignores the answer. Changes cannot be discarded except by not saving afterwards. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Escape in the raw policy editor looks like a cancel, but every edit has already changed the loaded policy source and the caller ignores the answer. Changes cannot be discarded except by not saving afterwards.

t: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run. Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run. Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.

t: Opening a live registry source tests writing by creating then deleting a probe value. A failure in between leaves the probe value behind, and the failure is swallowed. Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent
l: Opening a live registry source tests writing by creating then deleting a probe value. A failure in between leaves the probe value behind, and the failure is swallowed.

t: Reading a policy file trusts the length stored in each entry and the shape of the data. A damaged or hostile file can demand huge memory or fail unexplained, and REG files report no line number on error. Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
l: Reading a policy file trusts the length stored in each entry and the shape of the data. A damaged or hostile file can demand huge memory or fail unexplained, and REG files report no line number on error.

t: Several windows raise an unhandled error on ordinary input: double-clicking with no row selected, right-clicking with no category, an unnamed list entry, an unreadable import file, a malformed search wildcard, a removed product in a filter, or an inspector item with no match. No program-wide handler is set, so the framework's default error dialog appears. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: Several windows raise an unhandled error on ordinary input: double-clicking with no row selected, right-clicking with no category, an unnamed list entry, an unreadable import file, a malformed search wildcard, a removed product in a filter, or an inspector item with no match. No program-wide handler is set, so the framework's default error dialog appears.

t: The program permits TLS 1.0 and 1.1 alongside 1.2 for every web request it makes, which is only the template download; a comment gives Vista compatibility as the reason. A connection uses the best version both ends offer, but a server or on-path party forcing an old version would be accepted. Data is protected by weak or fixed encryption
l: The program permits TLS 1.0 and 1.1 alongside 1.2 for every web request it makes, which is only the template download; a comment gives Vista compatibility as the reason. A connection uses the best version both ends offer, but a server or on-path party forcing an old version would be accepted.

t: The program targets .NET Framework 4.5.2, which Microsoft stopped supporting in April 2022, so it gets no security fixes. The readme says newer versions also work and ship with Windows 10 or later, which limits the reach to the declared minimum. A technology is out of support or no longer receives fixes
l: The program targets .NET Framework 4.5.2, which Microsoft stopped supporting in April 2022, so it gets no security fixes. The readme says newer versions also work and ship with Windows 10 or later, which limits the reach to the declared minimum.

t: The template download uses one fixed address naming a single dated Windows 11 package (26H2) and its folder layout, with no fallback. When Microsoft retires it, or a newer release appears, the feature fails until the program is rebuilt. Releasing or running the system depends on manual or missing steps
l: The template download uses one fixed address naming a single dated Windows 11 package (26H2) and its folder layout, with no fallback. When Microsoft retires it, or a newer release appears, the feature fails until the program is rebuilt.

t: When a download, unpack or move fails, the person sees only which step failed, not the cause. The scratch folder is removed only on success, and files already moved into the destination are not rolled back. Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
l: When a download, unpack or move fails, the person sees only which step failed, not the cause. The scratch folder is removed only on success, and files already moved into the destination are not rolled back.

t: The foundation Contracts Domain Database API service UI components Web app End-to-end tests Tooling Carried by apps/api: the Bun service runs on the person's own Windows machine and reads, writes and lists folders (POL files, template folders, export targets) directly with Bun and node:fs; the web app asks it through the HttpApi contract and never touches disk. Carried by apps/api: reads and writes policy keys, and loads and unloads user hives, by running reg.exe and PowerShell from Bun on the person's machine, behind one registry port that the domain layer sees only as plain data. Carried by apps/api: reads ADMX and ADML files from the chosen folders through the file system carrier and hands their text to the pure parsers in packages/domain; schemas for the parsed result live in packages/contracts. Replaced by the Preference store: remembered choices (language, definitions folder, offers considered) are rows in PostgreSQL through Drizzle in packages/database, reached by apps/api; the old registry key is not read or written. Replaced: the Git version is stamped at build time by a script in packages/tooling that writes it into an environment value the API reports, instead of generating and compiling a version source file. Carried by apps/api: reads and writes CMTX files beside the policy sources through the file system carrier, with the XML encoding and decoding in packages/domain. Carried by apps/api: resolves user and group accounts and their profile and policy-object locations by calling the machine's own Windows directory tools (PowerShell and ADSI) from Bun, on the person's machine, and returns a plain result or an unavailable status when no domain is reachable. Carried by apps/api: downloads the policy template package with Bun fetch from the Microsoft download site, extracts it into the chosen folder through the file system carrier, and reports progress and failure through the contract; the web app never calls the site itself. Only the stack's libraries, plus fast-xml-parser (ADMX, ADML and CMTX XML in packages/domain), a small zip reader (fflate) in apps/api for the Microsoft template package, and Effect's own Schema, HttpApi, SQL and Layer modules for every service seam; no state library beyond TanStack Query and Form. Bun runs scripts and the API, Turborepo orchestrates one task name per layer (lint, typecheck, test, build) cached by inputs, TypeScript is strict with project references, configuration comes from typed environment values read once through Effect Config, and the app targets Windows 10 and 11 only, run locally as api plus web. Vitest for domain, contracts, database and api with fixture text for ADMX, ADML, POL and REG files; database tests run against a real PostgreSQL started by the test task, never a mock; Windows-only carriers are tested against fakes behind their ports plus a few Windows-gated tests; e2e is Playwright with axe against the running product, written before the code it tests; every rule and story carries its legacy rule as a test name. Behaviour lives in code and tests, not prose: contract schemas carry doc annotations that feed the OpenAPI document, each domain folder has a short README-free index with typed exports, rule names in test titles cite the legacy rule, and AGENTS.md holds only what code and tools do not show; decisions with trade-offs are kept in the plan, not copied into source. Every request, response and error is an Effect Schema; define it once here and generate the OpenAPI document from the HttpApi, never write the document by hand. An outside system being absent or failing (no domain, no network, no admin rights) is a tagged result in the schema, not a thrown error or an HTTP 500. Do not import from any other workspace package; contracts depend only on effect. No I/O, clock, randomness or environment access: functions take data in and return data or Effect values of data; outside systems arrive as ports declared here and implemented in apps/api. One folder per capability, named as in the plan; shared helpers go in a folder named for what they do, never utils or common. Parse ADMX, ADML, CMTX, POL and REG text into schema-checked values at the edge; downstream rules never see raw XML or bytes. Change the schema only through a Drizzle Kit migration that is committed; never edit a generated migration after it is merged. Queries are Effect SQL functions returning contract types' data shapes; callers never receive Drizzle table objects. Tests run against a real PostgreSQL with migrations applied from empty; no mocked client. Handlers are thin: decode with the contract, call domain functions and carriers, encode; rules never live in a handler. Each outside system (file system, registry, directory, download) is one Effect Layer implementing a domain port; the Windows ones have an in-memory fake used in tests and non-Windows runs. Spawn reg.exe and PowerShell with an argument array, never a built shell string, and validate key paths and account names against the contract schema first. Writes to a policy file go to a temporary file and are renamed over the target so a failed save never leaves a half-written file. Components take data and callbacks only, never call the API or router; each has a Storybook story covering its states, with an axe check. Use Tailwind 4 design tokens and the shadcn on Base UI primitives; do not add colors, spacing or icon sets outside them. Fetch through TanStack Query using a client generated from the contract; no hand-written fetch calls or duplicated response types. Every visible string is a Paraglide message; no literals in components, and policy text from definitions is shown as data, not translated. Forms use TanStack Form with the contract schema as the validator, so client and server reject the same input. Server rendering must not touch the machine: only the API reads disk or registry, and route loaders call it over HTTP. Write each test from the story's acceptance criteria and commit it before the code; it fails first, and runs against the real api with fake Windows carriers. Every page visited is scanned with axe, and a violation fails the test. Select elements by role and accessible name, never by CSS class or test id unless no role exists. Layers extend the shared configs here and add no local lint or format rules; a rule change is made here once. Commits follow conventional commits and lefthook runs lint, format and the affected layers' checks before commit; skipping hooks is not allowed. knip must pass with no unused files, exports or dependencies in any layer.

t: Read and write folders and policy files on the person's machine The service reads, lists and writes folders and files (policy files, template folders, export targets) directly so the browser never touches the disk. The program must edit real policy files at fixed Windows paths, which a browser cannot do.
l: Read and write folders and policy files on the person's machine

t: Read and write registry policies and user hives safely The service reads and writes policy keys, and loads and unloads user hives, through one registry port that the rules see only as plain data. Registry editing must work on Home editions without a compiled add-on and must not allow typed keys to run commands.
l: Read and write registry policies and user hives safely

t: Look up accounts and policy locations in the Active Directory domain The service resolves user and group accounts and their profile and policy-object locations from the machine's own directory tools, or says the domain is unavailable. Only the person's machine is joined to the domain with their credentials, and a missing domain is a normal outcome.
l: Look up accounts and policy locations in the Active Directory domain

t: Download and unpack the Microsoft policy template package The service downloads the package from the Microsoft download site, unpacks it into the chosen folder and reports progress and failure. The package must be unpacked into a Windows folder, which a browser cannot do, and having no internet is a normal outcome.
l: Download and unpack the Microsoft policy template package

t: Build the shared interface components with Storybook A library of shared screen components that take data and callbacks only, shown in Storybook, using the approved design tokens. One visual language and proven accessibility across all screens.
l: Build the shared interface components with Storybook

t: Build the web app shell, data access, messages and forms The screens' frame: server-rendered routes that fetch through the generated client, show every visible text as a translatable message, and validate forms with the contract. Screens must stay unprivileged, speak the person's chosen language and reject the same input as the service.
l: Build the web app shell, data access, messages and forms

t: Set up end-to-end tests with accessibility scans A Playwright suite that drives the running product with stand-in Windows carriers, scans every page and finds elements the way a person does. Stories are proven by behaviour, accessibility is a gate and tests stay deterministic without Windows.
l: Set up end-to-end tests with accessibility scans

t: Stamp the program with its Git version at build time The build records the current Git version in a value the service reports, in place of generating a version source file. The new build has no compile step needing a generated file, and a committed generated file goes stale.
l: Stamp the program with its Git version at build time

t: Share one set of code checks and commit rules across layers One shared setup for linting, formatting, unused-code checks, markdown checks and commit messages, run before every commit. One policy for every layer, and early failure beats failing in CI.
l: Share one set of code checks and commit rules across layers

t: Load policy definitions from a folder o...: Template file source adapter Read the administrative template and language files from a chosen folder, or add a single template file, and build the policies and categories people browse. People can only browse and edit policies once their definitions are loaded, and they need to know when something in them could not be used. Definitions
l: Load policy definitions from a folder o...: Template file source adapter

t: Show the category tree and the policies of the chosen area Present the categories of the loaded definitions as a tree with icons, visibility, selection, and a choice of user or computer area. People find a policy by walking the categories, so the tree must show the right ones and keep their place as it changes. Empty category
l: Show the category tree and the policies of the chosen area

t: Read and write policy files byte for byte Turn the bytes of a policy file into entries and entries back into bytes, with its signature, version, text and number encodings, ordering and duplicate handling. Policy files are what Windows reads, so a file saved here must be read back exactly and a bad file must be refused with a clear message. Policy file
l: Read and write policy files byte for byte

t: Hold a policy file's settings in memory and answer questions about them Keep the entries of one policy file and answer whether a value is present, read it, set it, forget it, mark it for deletion or clear a key. Applying policies and checking what a file says depend on these answers being exact, including what is marked for deletion. Marked for deletion
l: Hold a policy file's settings in memory and answer questions about them

t: Read and write the machine's live policy settings Read, write, delete and clear the live policy settings of the machine, check the root names and test whether they can be written. People apply policies straight to the machine, so this source must behave as the machine's own settings do. Live settings
l: Read and write the machine's live policy settings

t: Open another user's stored settings file as a source Load a user's stored settings file into the machine under a temporary name and unload it when the source is released. People can edit the policies of a user who is not signed in, and the machine must be left as it was. User hive
l: Open another user's stored settings file as a source

t: Export settings to a registry text file Collect the settings destined for an exported registry text file, limited to a branch, and refuse every read or check. l: Export settings to a registry text file

t: Apply one policy file's changes onto another source When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, each entry is saved, deleted or cleared as the file says, and values a newer file dropped are forgotten. Administrators can bring one policy file's settings into another source and trust that deletions and removals carry over exactly. Marker-style entry
l: Apply one policy file's changes onto another source

t: Choose an exported settings file and have its key prefix worked out A person starts an import by choosing an exported machine-settings file. The system checks the file is a genuine export, reads its keys, removals, deletions and values, works out the key prefix from the first key, and warns when the file holds default values or the prefix could not be worked out. The person gives a prefix only when none was worked out. The person brings settings from another machine without typing a prefix by hand, and learns at once when the file is not a genuine export or the prefix is unknown. The person can also close the import window with Escape. Exported settings file Key prefix Default value Top-level section
l: Choose an exported settings file and have its key prefix worked out

t: Bring the exported settings into the chosen policy source Once a file and a prefix are settled, the person imports the settings into the chosen policy source: marked keys are cleared, marked values are deleted and the others are saved with the prefix left off their names, and what the person sees is refreshed. The settings from the exported file end up in the policy source the person chose, and a failure is reported plainly instead of leaving the person guessing.
